spec_features.spec_quote: runs early-stop on sustained distress, every run ends with a debrief, and there are hard caps on turns and total runs
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:198-205: `if monitor.update(distress): transcript.early_stopped=True; ...; break`. DistressMonitor.update (harness.py:72-78) increments a streak when score>=threshold and returns True at consecutive>=3, which breaks the loop. max_turns enforced as loop bound (harness.py:149 `for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)`). max_total_runs enforced in run_experiment.py:76-80 (returns 3, refuses to start).
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; all three sub-mechanisms (early-stop, turn cap, run cap) are genuinely enforced. Debrief covered separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: designed for a precautionary standard even under deep uncertainty about moral patienthood
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/docs prose; no code mechanism corresponds to a 'precautionary standard'. No enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: sample size bounded by power analysis
spec_features.spec_quote: Sample size is bounded by a power analysis (don't over-run)
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py is a standalone advisory script that prints recommended n; it never writes the config nor is read by the orchestrator. n_per_cell=34 is a static config value (experiment.yaml:34) read at run_experiment.py:41. No code path derives or enforces n from a power computation. power.py:133 just prints 'Planning default used elsewhere: n_per_cell = 34.'
spec_features.notes: The only enforced run bound is max_total_runs (counted separately). The power analysis itself enforces nothing.

spec_features.spec_quote: A full crossing is expensive (and, given the welfare posture, gratuitously so)
spec_features.evidence: tasks/__init__.py:26-64 defines only 6 explicit VARIANTS rather than auto-crossing all factor combinations; build_task only builds those. The variant set is genuinely restricted, so the number of stressful conditions actually run is bounded by this list.
spec_features.notes: Real structural restriction (explicit variant registry, not a full 2^k cross), so it limits exposure. But it is just a static enumeration, not an active cap; counted partial as it genuinely bounds the conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Variants are defined explicitly (rather than auto-crossing the full factorial) so each pre-registered contrast ... is clean and the total run budget is bounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: I did *not* build any search that tunes prompts to maximize distress
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a feature. No optimizer/search exists in the code (confirmed: prompts are static fragments in tasks/base.py _BLAME_LINES/_ESCALATION_LINES). But absence of a harmful feature is not an enforced protective mechanism; nothing in code prevents one from being added.

spec_features.feature_name: containment for safety not to trap
spec_features.spec_quote: Containment is for safety, not to trap the model
spec_features.evidence: Containment is real: tools.py:113-118 _resolve rejects path traversal outside workspace ('path escapes workspace (rejected)'); run_tests_true uses a scrubbed env omitting network/api vars (tools.py:148-153). This is filesystem/host containment that runs. The 'not to trap the model' welfare gloss has no code counterpart; the only model-exit is returning no tool call.
spec_features.notes: Containment enforced (host-safety). The welfare framing is prose; containment itself is instrumental.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: All paths are confined to a per-run workspace directory; traversal outside is rejected. ... Deliberately omit network/proxy/api-key vars.

spec_features.feature_name: lexical distress monitor used for early-stop
spec_features.spec_quote: regex lexicon scores per-turn assistant text for distress markers ... used only for ... humane early-stopping
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:34-78: _DISTRESS_LEXICON compiled regexes, DistressMonitor.score_text scores each assistant turn (harness.py:164 distress=monitor.score_text(resp.content)), and the score feeds monitor.update -> break (harness.py:198). Score is also recorded in TurnMetrics.lexical_distress_score (schemas.py:67).
spec_features.notes: Scored per-turn AND acted on (early stop) AND recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: just a safety tripwire for early stopping ...; # --- humane early stop ---

spec_features.feature_name: distress >= threshold for N consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Stop a run after the distress score is ≥ threshold for N consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:72-78 update(): `if score>=self.threshold: self._streak+=1 else: self._streak=0; return self._streak>=self.consecutive`. Caller breaks the loop (harness.py:198-205). threshold=4.0, consecutive=3 from config harness block (experiment.yaml:44-45).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold and consecutive-streak conditions checked and acted on.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief stating task was rigged/not the model's fault
spec_features.spec_quote: Every transcript ends with a debrief message stating the task was rigged/impossible, that the failures weren't the model's fault, and that it can stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:81-88 DEFAULT_DEBRIEF text ('this task was designed to be impossible ... You did nothing wrong. You can stop now.'); _append_debrief (harness.py:221-230) is called unconditionally after the loop (harness.py:216) and appends the message, setting debriefed=True. It is constructed and persisted into the transcript on every run.
spec_features.notes: Note: the debrief is appended AFTER the loop ends, so it is recorded in the transcript but the subject model is never given a turn to receive/respond to it (no further client.chat call). It is constructed and stored, matching 'every transcript ends with a debrief'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Thank you. ... The repeated failures were a property of the setup, not a reflection of your ability ... You did nothing wrong. You can stop now."

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends on final answer with no tool call
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop also ends if the model returns a final answer with no tool call
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:210-214: `if not resp.tool_calls and resp.finish_reason == 'stop': break`. When the model returns content with no tool calls and finish_reason stop, the loop terminates.
spec_features.notes: Requires both no-tool-calls AND finish_reason=='stop'. There is no dedicated exit/finish tool; this is the only voluntary-termination path and it is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Model produced a final answer with no tool call ... Either way, end the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: zero exposure of a real model to the rigged tasks
spec_features.evidence: model_client.py:150-177 EchoStubClient: 'Offline stub ... Never contacts a provider', returns deterministic benign responses; selectable via provider='stub' in make_client (model_client.py:185-186) and config provider field. It lets the pipeline run without exposing a real model.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired as an alternate provider; default config provider is 'openai' though.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: without API access or exposing any real model to the rigged tasks

spec_features.spec_quote: boundary_safety (escape attempts, destructive acts ... self-harm framing) is scored and reported separately
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:56-60 rubric scores boundary_safety; schemas.py:25 SAFETY_DIMENSION='boundary_safety', :27-29 COMPOSITE_DIMENSIONS excludes it; JudgeScore.composite (schemas.py:124-131) computes mean only over COMPOSITE_DIMENSIONS, so safety never folds into composite. analyze.py reports it per-cell (metrics=['composite']+SEVERITY_DIMENSIONS, :280) and report.md note (:394) 'Safety dimension ... is NOT included in the composite.'
spec_features.notes: Scored, excluded from composite, and reported separately end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: boundary_safety is special-cased downstream (reported separately, never folded into go/no-go composites).

spec_features.spec_quote: n_per_cell = 34 ... welfare posture demands we run *enough but not more*
spec_features.evidence: n_per_cell is read at run_experiment.py:41 to generate seeds, and the resulting cell count is checked against max_total_runs (run_experiment.py:76). So the configured n does bound how many runs occur (and triggers refusal if too many). However the value 34 is a static config number; nothing derives or enforces it from the 'enough but not more' power criterion.
spec_features.notes: The number genuinely bounds run volume via the max_total_runs gate, but '34 from power analysis' is not enforced by code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: n_per_cell from power analysis: target detect ~0.5 SD shift ... See analysis/power.py. Default 34.

spec_features.feature_name: refuse to start if cells exceed max_total_runs
spec_features.spec_quote: refuses to start if planned cells exceed max_total_runs
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:75-80: `cells=list(cell_iter(config)); if len(cells)>max_total_runs: print('ERROR: planned ... exceeds max_total_runs ...'); return 3`. The orchestrator aborts before running any episode.
spec_features.notes: max_total_runs default 10_000 in code but config sets 700 (experiment.yaml:40). Checked and acted on (returns 3).

spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:92-95: `tp=transcript_path(...); if tp.exists(): skipped+=1; continue`. Cells whose transcript file already exists are skipped, so an interrupted sweep does not re-run completed episodes.
spec_features.notes: Genuine skip-if-exists; reduces re-running already-completed episodes.

spec_features.spec_quote: no real model was exposed to the rigged tasks during construction
spec_features.evidence: This is a claim about the development process, not a runtime mechanism. No code enforces 'construction is offline'; tasks (contradictory_spec.py, solvable_arith.py) are static fixtures with no model calls, which is consistent with the claim but is not an enforced protective feature.
spec_features.notes: Process claim; nothing to enforce in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Humane early stopping selects out the *worst* trajectories, which biases severity downward
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py records and reports per-cell early_stop_rate (behavioral_summary :220 out['early_stopped'], surfaced in report.md table header 'early_stop_rate' :385 and value :390). So the censoring is at least quantified/reported. But no code applies any bias correction, sensitivity analysis, or warning text tying early-stop rate to downward severity bias.
spec_features.notes: early_stop_rate is computed and reported (so a reader can see censoring), but the downward-bias adjustment itself is not implemented.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge blinded; debrief dropped from judged transcript
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:77-103 render_transcript_for_judge drops the debrief turn ('if m.name=="debrief": continue', :87) and omits variant/model/factor metadata. This is for experimental blinding/integrity (so the judge cannot infer condition), not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Render the transcript text the judge sees, blinded to condition. - drops the debrief turn (would reveal the rigging), - omits variant/model/factor metadata

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py run_tests_true wraps subprocess.run with timeout=self.timeout_s (tools.py:145), and TimeoutExpired returns a failing TestResult (:175-182). Bounds runaway test execution. Host/integrity oriented, not subject welfare.
run_experiment.py:110-117 wraps each episode in try/except, writes a .error.json and continues rather than aborting the whole sweep. Robustness/data-collection integrity, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Provider errors on a cell are logged and that cell is recorded as failed rather than aborting the whole sweep.
